title: System Failure Modes: Resource Exhaustion & Cascade Recovery
purpose: Visualizes the critical failure mechanics of Linux OS resource exhaustion (EMFILE file descriptor saturation and 100% inode depletion) inside a production compute instance.
routing_rationale: When application workloads experience unexpected traffic surges, kernel-level limits (ulimit -n) reject new connection sockets. If unhandled errors trigger uncontrolled debug logging, filesystem inode exhaustion locks the persistent disk into read-only mode.

nodes.label: Client Traffic Burst
nodes.detail: Spike of 50,000 concurrent HTTP requests hitting the Compute Engine instance.

nodes.label: Web Server Daemon
nodes.detail: Accepts client TCP connections and delegates request processing to worker threads.

nodes.label: Error Log (/var/log)
nodes.detail: Captures unthrottled verbose application stack traces and debug dumps during cascading failures.

nodes.label: ulimit -n (FD Limit)
nodes.detail: Limits maximum open file descriptors (sockets, files, pipes) per process; default is often 1024.

nodes.label: Disk Inode Table
nodes.detail: Fixed metadata table tracking file pointers; exhausting inodes causes 'No space left on device' even with free disk bytes.

steps.title: Traffic Surge & Socket Descriptor Allocation
steps.action: Flash crowd or retry storm floods Web Server Daemon with 50,000 concurrent TCP connection attempts.
steps.why_traversal: Each active HTTP connection requires a dedicated socket file descriptor allocated by the Linux kernel.
steps.narration: Step 1: Sudden traffic surge directs thousands of concurrent client connections to the web server process.

steps.title: File Descriptor Ceiling Reached (EMFILE Error)
steps.action: Web server reaches default ulimit -n ceiling (1024); kernel syscall accept4() returns errno 24 (EMFILE: Too many open files).
steps.why_traversal: Linux kernel enforces strict per-process file descriptor limits to prevent single processes from exhausting global kernel memory.
steps.narration: Step 2: Process exhausts allocated file descriptors; kernel immediately rejects subsequent socket() and accept() calls.

check.logs: nginx: [emerg] socket() failed (24: Too many open files)

steps.title: Cascading Error Logging & Disk I/O Saturation
steps.action: Application catches unhandled connection failures and writes verbose stack traces to /var/log/app/error.log at 10,000 lines/second.
steps.why_traversal: Unthrottled error logging generates massive write I/O amplification, saturating virtual persistent disk IOPS and storage bandwidth.
steps.protocol: POSIX write() Syscall / Ext4 Write Queue
steps.narration: Step 3: Unhandled failure cascade triggers emergency error logging, hammering persistent disk write IOPS.

steps.title: Filesystem Inode Table Depletion (100% Inodes)
steps.action: Micro-log creation exhausts 100% of available filesystem inodes; kernel marks filesystem read-only, rejecting all writes despite gigabytes of free disk space.
steps.why_traversal: Ext4/XFS filesystems allocate a finite inode table at format time. Even a 0-byte file requires one inode.
steps.protocol: Ext4 Inode Allocation Block / VFS Read-Only Lock
steps.narration: Step 4: Millions of error files exhaust the filesystem inode table; kernel puts disk in read-only mode to prevent corruption.

check.logs: kernel: EXT4-fs error: no free inode; remounting read-only

steps.title: Live prlimit Elevation & Automated Remediation
steps.action: Automated SRE remediation script detects saturation, executes prlimit --pid=<pid> --nofile=65536:65536 live, and purges micro-logs.
steps.why_traversal: prlimit allows modifying running process resource ceilings without restarting the daemon, restoring connection capacity immediately.
steps.narration: Step 5: Live prlimit call expands process file descriptor ceiling to 65,536; logrotate prunes orphan logs and normal traffic resumes.

check.logs: prlimit applied; file descriptor ceiling updated to 65536

scenarios.label: 100% Inode Exhaustion Outage (Silent Lockup)
scenarios.narration: Unrotated session files or debug logs consume every filesystem inode. df -h shows 50GB free, but applications crash with 'No space left on device'.
scenarios.root_cause: Missing logrotate configuration and rapid generation of millions of small temporary files.
scenarios.path_divergence: System cannot write PID files, locks, or database journals. Daemon panics and system monitoring scripts fail to record data.
scenarios.blast_radius: Entire Compute Engine VM instance. All resident daemons crash or enter read-only degraded state.
scenarios.durable_prevention: Configure daily logrotate with maxsize 100M and maxage 7; set up Cloud Monitoring metric disk/inode_used_percent > 85%.

scenarios.label: EMFILE Socket Rejection Cascade
scenarios.narration: High-traffic web proxy hits system default ulimit -n ceiling of 1024 open files. Inbound TCP handshakes stall, triggering 502 Bad Gateway across upstream load balancers.
scenarios.root_cause: systemd unit file omitted LimitNOFILE directive; inherited default soft limit of 1024 from parent init environment.
scenarios.path_divergence: Incoming connections sit in TCP listen backlog queue until backlog fills, dropping subsequent SYN packets.
scenarios.blast_radius: All incoming user traffic routed through this web proxy instance.
scenarios.durable_prevention: Add LimitNOFILE=65535 to [Service] block in systemd unit file and set /etc/security/limits.conf system-wide.

scenarios.label: Quota exhausted
scenarios.root_cause: A project or regional quota reaches its allocation limit.
scenarios.diverted_path: Requests surface elevated latency, errors, or denied actions.
scenarios.blast_radius: Consumers of the affected resource or dependency.
scenarios.recovery: Reduce load, restore the dependency, and add a tested prevention.

summary: Visualizes the critical failure mechanics of Linux OS resource exhaustion (EMFILE file descriptor saturation and 100% inode depletion) inside a production compute instance.
